title: Heating fault
causes: A fault in the heating part of the circulation (heat) pump.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher at the fuse or breaker for 30 seconds.
Switch back on and start a programme.
technician: If the code returns, call Bosch service.

title: Limescale on the heating pump
causes: Limescale has built up on the heat pump, often in hard-water areas.
steps: Run a descaling cycle with a dishwasher descaler.
Keep the softening salt topped up if your model has a water softener.
Descale regularly if you have hard water.
technician: If the code continues after descaling, call Bosch service.

title: Water filling problem (flow meter)
causes: The flow meter has failed or the dishwasher is not filling correctly.
steps: Check the water tap under the sink is fully open.
Switch off at the breaker for 30 seconds and try again.
technician: Bosch advises contacting service for this code.

title: Water in the base pan (leak protection activated)
causes: Water has collected in the base of the dishwasher.
A leak from a hose, seal or internal part.
Too much foam, for example from washing-up liquid.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Turn off the water tap to the dishwasher.
Wipe up any water on the floor.
technician: Bosch advises turning off the water and calling service. A hidden leak needs to be found and fixed.

title: Water may not be entering
causes: The inlet hose is kinked or damaged.
steps: Check the inlet hose is not bent, squashed or damaged.
Make sure the water tap is open.
technician: If the code continues, call Bosch service.

title: Water may not be entering
causes: The inlet hose is kinked or damaged.
steps: Check the inlet hose is not bent, squashed or damaged.
Make sure the water tap is open.
technician: If the code continues, call Bosch service.

title: Water level too low
causes: The water tap is closed or partly closed.
The inlet hose is kinked.
Low water flow.
steps: Make sure the water supply is fully on.
Check the inlet hose for kinks or damage.
Check the flow: the tap should give about 10 litres per minute.
technician: If the supply is fine and the code returns, call Bosch service.

title: Detergent dispenser circuit fault
causes: An electrical fault in the detergent dispenser circuit.
steps: Switch off at the breaker for 30 seconds, then on again.
technician: If the code returns, call Bosch service.

title: Filter blocked
causes: Food scraps are blocking the filter.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher.
Remove the bottom basket and lift out the filter.
Rinse the filter under running water with a soft brush and mild soap.
Refit the filter until it locks in place.
technician: Not usually needed. If the code stays after cleaning, call Bosch service.

title: Drain pump blocked or faulty
causes: The drain pump is clogged or has failed.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Clean the filter and check for loose debris in the sump.
technician: Bosch advises calling service for this code.

title: Not draining – drain hose or filter blocked
causes: The drain hose is kinked or blocked.
The filter is blocked.
A new waste disposer or sink trap still has its blanking plug in.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Check the drain hose for kinks.
Clean the filters and make sure the pump cover under the filter is fitted.
If the dishwasher is connected to a waste disposer or new sink trap, check the blanking plug was removed.
technician: If it still will not drain, call Bosch service.

title: Drain pump blocked or pump cover loose
causes: Broken glass, seeds or other debris are blocking the drain pump.
The pump cover is loose or missing.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Remove the bottom basket and the filters.
Scoop out standing water with a cup or sponge.
Unclip the white pump cover (a spoon helps) and remove debris. Watch for sharp glass.
Refit the cover until it clicks, then refit the filters.
technician: If the code returns after cleaning, call Bosch service.

title: Mains voltage too low
causes: The home power supply voltage is too low. The dishwasher itself is not faulty.
steps: Switch off at the breaker for 30 seconds, then on again.
technician: If it happens again, have an electrician check the supply voltage.

title: Water level too low in the wash
causes: Bowls or pots have tipped over and are holding water.
Dishes are blocking the water intake.
steps: Check the load and turn bowls and pots face down.
Make sure nothing blocks the spray arms or intake.
technician: If it repeats, contact Siemens service.

title: Heating system fault
causes: A fault in the heating system.
steps: Switch off, wait a few minutes and switch on again.
technician: Contact Siemens service and quote the code.

title: Heater covered in limescale or dirt
causes: Limescale or dirt on the heating element.
steps: Run a descaling cycle as described in the user manual.
Clean the filters.
technician: If the code continues after descaling, contact Siemens service.

title: Filling fault – water protection active
causes: A problem with the water supply or filling system.
steps: Check the water tap is open.
Check the inlet hose is not kinked.
technician: If it repeats, contact Siemens service.

title: Water in the base (water protection activated)
causes: Water has collected in the base tray of the dishwasher.
steps: Close the water tap.
Switch off the dishwasher.
Wipe up any water on the floor.
technician: Siemens advises not repairing this yourself. Call Siemens service.

title: Filling or water inflow fault
causes: A problem with the filling system or water inflow.
steps: Turn off the tap.
Check the inlet hose for kinks, then turn the tap back on.
technician: If it happens often, the appliance needs an engineer. Contact Siemens service.

title: Water inlet fault
causes: The inlet hose is bent.
The tap is closed, stuck or furred with limescale.
The inlet filter is clogged.
steps: Make sure the tap is fully open.
Check the inlet hose for kinks.
Switch off, close the tap, remove the hose and clean the filter, then refit and check for leaks.
technician: If water flow is low, call a plumber. If it repeats, contact Siemens service.

title: Filters dirty or blocked
causes: Food scraps are clogging the filter system.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher.
Take out the filters and rinse them clean.
Refit the filters correctly.
technician: Not usually needed.

title: Drain pump fault
causes: A fault with the waste water pump.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Siemens says only its service can fix this. Contact them and quote the code.

title: Not draining – likely blocked pump or hose
causes: The drain pump or drain path is blocked.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Clean the filters and check for debris in the pump area.
Check the drain hose is not kinked.
technician: If the problem persists, close the tap and call Siemens service.

title: Drain pump blocked
causes: Debris such as glass or seeds is blocking the drain pump.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Remove the filters and scoop out standing water.
Remove the pump cover and clear debris carefully – watch for sharp glass.
Refit the cover and filters.
technician: If the problem persists, close the tap and call Siemens service.

title: Low mains voltage
causes: The power supply voltage is too low. The appliance itself is not faulty.
steps: Switch off and on again later.
technician: Have an electrician check your supply. If it recurs, contact Siemens service.

title: Little or no water coming in
causes: The water valve is closed.
The water supply is off.
The inlet hose or valve is frozen or blocked.
steps: Check the water valve is fully open.
Check there is water at other taps.
Check the inlet hose is not kinked or blocked.
technician: If water still does not enter, contact Samsung service.

title: Water not draining
causes: The drain or sink connection is blocked.
The filter is clogged.
The drain hose is kinked.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Clean the mesh filter in the base.
Check the drain hose and sink connection for kinks or blockages.
technician: If it still will not drain, contact Samsung service.

title: Drain pump stalls
causes: Debris is jamming the drain pump.
steps: Cancel the cycle to drain.
Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Remove the lower rack and filter, and check the sump for debris.
technician: If the pump still stalls, contact Samsung service.

title: Leak detected
causes: Water is leaking around the door or into the base.
Washing-up liquid used instead of dishwasher detergent.
The sink or waste disposer is backing up.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher.
Use only dishwasher detergent.
Clean the door seal and the bottom edge of the door.
Check under the dishwasher for water and wipe it up.
Check the sink drain is not backing up.
technician: If water keeps leaking, turn off the water supply and contact Samsung service.

title: Overfill or too much foam
causes: Too much detergent foam.
A blocked filter.
The drain hose is kinked.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher.
Check you are using the right dishwasher detergent and amount.
Clean the filter and remove standing water from the base.
Check the drain hose for kinks.
technician: If the dishwasher keeps filling, turn off the water supply and contact Samsung service.

title: Heating problem (too hot)
causes: The inlet water is very hot.
Filters are dirty, so water does not circulate well.
steps: Switch off for at least 5 minutes.
Clean the filters.
Run a normal cycle with an empty dishwasher and detergent.
technician: If the code returns, contact Samsung service.

title: Temperature sensor problem
causes: The dishwasher detected a temperature sensing fault.
steps: Switch off at the wall or breaker for at least 5 minutes.
Switch on and run a Normal cycle.
technician: If the code returns, contact Samsung service.

title: Door not closed
causes: The door is not latched.
A utensil or dish sticks out and blocks the door.
steps: Push in any items that stick out.
Clean the door latch area.
Close the door firmly.
Switch off for 30 seconds, then on again.
technician: If the door will not latch, contact Samsung service.

title: Wash pump not running
causes: The dishwasher fills but the wash motor does not start.
steps: Switch off for one minute, then try again.
technician: If there is still no spraying, contact Samsung service.

title: Will not start with Zone Wash or Half Load
causes: A fault linked to the Zone Wash or Half Load feature.
steps: Switch off for at least 30 seconds.
Turn off Zone Wash or Half Load and run a Normal cycle.
technician: If the code returns, contact Samsung service.

title: Voltage protection mode
causes: A power flicker, surge or tripped breaker.
steps: Check the plug and socket.
Switch off at the wall or breaker for at least 1 minute, then try again.
Use a dedicated socket without extension leads or adapters.
technician: If it keeps happening, have an electrician check the supply.

title: Powers on but will not run
causes: An internal control fault.
steps: Switch off at the wall or breaker.
Wait 1 minute, switch on and try again.
technician: If the code returns, contact Samsung service.

title: Detergent dispenser problem
causes: The dispenser motor is not working normally.
A tablet is stuck in the dispenser.
steps: Unplug the dishwasher for 5 minutes.
Check that no tablet is stuck in the dispenser.
technician: If the code returns, contact Samsung service.

title: Leak or overfill detected
causes: Too much water came in, or a leak was found.
Washing-up liquid caused too much foam.
The dishwasher is not level.
steps: Use only dishwasher detergent.
Load big plates and pots face down.
Check the dishwasher is level.
technician: If there is no leak but the code stays, switch off power and request LG service. Do not pull out a built-in unit yourself.

title: Not enough water coming in
causes: Water cut in the home.
The inlet hose is bent or squashed.
The inlet or under-sink valve is closed.
steps: Check other taps have water.
Straighten the inlet hose and remove anything pressing on it.
Open the valve under the sink, especially after installation or moving.
technician: If it continues, contact the installer or LG service.

title: Not draining
causes: The filter is clogged.
The drain hose is bent or squashed.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher and wait 30 minutes for it to cool.
Remove the lower rack, twist out the filter and rinse it.
Refit the filter until it clicks.
Straighten the drain hose.
technician: If water keeps standing above the filter, request LG service.

title: Too much foam
causes: Washing-up liquid was used.
Too much detergent.
steps: Use only dishwasher detergent, and less of it.
Wipe out the foam and run a rinse cycle without detergent.
technician: If bE shows with no foam, request LG service.

title: Spray (Vario) pump problem
causes: The impeller is not turning normally.
Dishes are touching the spray system.
steps: Rearrange the dishes so nothing blocks the spray arms.
Restart the cycle.
technician: If the code persists, request LG service.

title: Water not heating
causes: A heater fault.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: LG advises requesting service.

title: Temperature sensor fault
causes: Poor contact or a failed temperature sensor.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: LG advises requesting service.

title: Wash motor fault
causes: The cleaning motor is not working properly.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: LG advises requesting service.

title: Water level sensor fault (older models)
causes: A fault in the water level sensor.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: LG advises requesting service.

title: Auto door opening not working
causes: Something is blocking the door.
A fault in the auto-open parts.
steps: Clear anything near the door and restart.
technician: If it continues, request LG service.

title: Not filling with water
causes: The water tap is closed.
Water pressure is too low.
The inlet hose is kinked.
The filter in the inlet hose is clogged.
steps: Open the water tap.
Check the inlet hose for kinks or bends.
Switch off and unplug the dishwasher, close the tap, remove the hose and clean its filter.
Refit the hose hand-tight, open the tap and run a programme.
technician: If it continues, contact an authorised service centre.

title: Not draining
causes: The sink spigot or trap is clogged.
The filter or sump is clogged.
The drain hose is kinked, too long or set at the wrong height.
After installation, the blanking plug was left in the sink trap.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Clean the filter and sump.
Check the drain hose is not kinked or twisted.
Check the sink trap spigot is clear (and the blanking plug removed after a new install).
Plug in and run a programme.
technician: If it still will not drain, contact an authorised service centre.

title: Leak detected (anti-flood)
causes: The anti-flood system found water in the base.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Close the water tap.
Wipe up any water on the floor.
technician: Book a repair to find and fix the leak.

title: Water level (pressure) sensor problem
causes: The water level cannot be measured correctly.
steps: Switch off at the socket for about one minute, then restart.
technician: If the code returns, book a repair.

title: Wash motor or circulation pump fault
causes: A fault in the wash motor, circulation pump or its control.
steps: Switch off at the socket for about one minute, then restart.
technician: If the code returns, book a repair.

title: Heating fault
causes: The water is not heating as expected.
steps: Switch off at the socket for about one minute, then restart.
technician: If the code returns, book a repair.

title: Water level control problem
causes: The fill level is wrong or abnormal.
steps: Check the water tap is fully open.
Clean the filters.
Switch off at the socket for about one minute, then restart.
technician: If the code returns, book a repair.

title: Anti-flood overflow
causes: Water in the base tripped the anti-flood float.
A leak or faulty float switch.
steps: Switch the dishwasher off and on to reset.
Close the water tap if water is on the floor.
technician: If it returns, book a Hotpoint engineer.

title: Water fill valve fault
causes: The fill valve lets water in when it should not, or has failed.
steps: Check the drain hose is not lying on the floor.
Close the water tap if water keeps entering.
technician: Book a Hotpoint engineer.

title: Drain fault / drain took too long
causes: The drain hose or under-sink plumbing is blocked.
The drain pump is blocked or faulty.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Clean the filters.
Check the drain hose and under-sink plumbing for blockages.
technician: If the fault continues, book an engineer.

title: Temperature sensor fault
causes: A fault in the thermostat or temperature sensor.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book a Hotpoint engineer.

title: Filling took too long
causes: The tap is closed or partly closed.
Low water pressure.
The fill hose is kinked or its filter is clogged.
steps: Make sure the tap is fully open.
Check the fill hose is not kinked or squashed.
Check the water pressure is normal.
technician: If the fault continues, book an engineer.

title: Water took too long to heat
causes: Limescale, too much foam, a wrong water hardness setting, or a heating fault.
steps: Check the water hardness setting.
Use the right amount of detergent.
technician: Book a Hotpoint engineer.

title: Heating element fault
causes: The heating circuit is open or the element has failed.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book a Hotpoint engineer.

title: Wash pump fault
causes: The wash pump has failed, seized or is jammed by debris.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Clean the filters.
technician: Book a Hotpoint engineer.

title: Main board and display not communicating
causes: A wiring or display fault.
steps: Unplug the dishwasher for 2 minutes, then plug in and test.
technician: If it persists, book an engineer.

title: Main board fault
causes: The main control board has failed.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book a Hotpoint engineer.

title: Anti-flood overflow
causes: Water in the base tripped the anti-flood system.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Close the water tap and wipe up any water.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Water fill valve fault
causes: The water fill valve has failed.
steps: Close the water tap if water keeps entering.
Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Drain fault / drain took too long
causes: A blockage in the drain hose or under-sink plumbing.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Clean the filters.
Check the drain hose and under-sink plumbing for blockages.
technician: If the fault continues, book an engineer.

title: Temperature sensor fault
causes: A fault in the thermostat or temperature sensor.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Filling took too long
causes: The tap is not fully open.
Low water pressure.
The fill hose is restricted.
steps: Make sure the tap is fully open.
Check the fill hose is not kinked or squashed.
Check there is normal water pressure.
technician: If the fault continues, book an engineer.

title: Water took too long to heat
causes: The temperature was not reached in time.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Heating element fault
causes: A fault in the heating element.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Wash pump fault
causes: The wash pump has failed.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Main board and display not communicating
causes: A communication fault between the control boards.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Main board fault
causes: The main control board has failed.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
technician: Book an Indesit engineer.

title: Water overflow or leak
causes: Too much water is entering the dishwasher.
A leak inside the machine.
steps: Let the dishwasher run its safety drain.
If the code clears, no action is needed.
If it stays, switch off, unplug and close the water tap.
technician: If E:01 stays on, the fault is permanent. Call Beko service.

title: Water supply cut off
causes: The mains water is off.
The inlet tap is closed.
steps: Make sure the water tap is open.
The programme waits and checks for water. It continues once water flows.
technician: If water is on and the code stays, call Beko service.

title: Water not pumping away
causes: The non-return valve or drain pump cover is not fitted correctly.
The drain pump is blocked by debris.
steps: Switch off and unplug the dishwasher.
Remove the lower spray arm (if fitted) and the filter combination.
Scoop out standing water with a small cup.
Take off the pump cover / non-return valve, rinse it and remove debris. Watch for glass splinters.
Check the pump impeller turns by hand, refit the cover until it clicks, then refit the filters.
technician: If F11 persists, contact Miele service.

title: Water inlet blocked or restricted
causes: The stopcock is not open.
The inlet filter is dirty.
The inlet hose is kinked.
Water pressure is below 0.5 bar.
steps: Open the stopcock fully.
Switch off and unplug, close the stopcock, unscrew the inlet valve and clean the small filter. Never put the valve housing in water – it holds an electrical part.
Refit the filter and valve, then slowly open the stopcock and check for drips.
Straighten any kinks in the hose.
technician: If pressure is too low, call a plumber. If the fault persists, contact Miele service.

title: Water inlet blocked or restricted
causes: The stopcock is closed.
The inlet filter is dirty.
The inlet hose is kinked.
Water pressure is below 0.5 bar.
steps: Open the stopcock fully.
Switch off and unplug, close the stopcock and clean the inlet filter. Do not dip the valve housing in water.
Refit, slowly reopen the stopcock and check for leaks.
Straighten any kinks in the hose.
technician: If pressure is too low, call a plumber. If the fault persists, contact Miele service.

title: Circulation pump or water intake fault
causes: The circulation pump has dried out and stuck after a long break.
A technical fault in a level switch.
steps: Remove the lower spray arm and filter combination.
Pour in 1 litre of warm water (max 75°C) with a few drops of rinse aid and wait 5 minutes.
Refit the filters and spray arm and restart. Repeat 2–3 times if needed.
Otherwise switch off, wait a few seconds, switch on and restart.
technician: If F14 persists, contact Miele service.

title: Water inlet blocked or restricted
causes: The stopcock is closed.
The inlet filter is dirty.
The inlet hose is kinked.
Water pressure is below 0.5 bar.
steps: Open the stopcock fully.
Switch off and unplug, close the stopcock and clean the inlet filter. Do not dip the valve housing in water.
Refit, slowly reopen the stopcock and check for leaks.
Straighten any kinks in the hose.
technician: If pressure is too low, call a plumber. If the fault persists, contact Miele service.

title: Water intake valve defective
causes: The water intake valve has failed.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher and close the stopcock.
technician: Miele says you cannot fix this yourself. Book a Miele technician.

title: Heating relay fault
causes: A contact fault in the heating relay.
steps: Switch off the dishwasher.
technician: Miele says you cannot fix this yourself. Book a Miele technician.

title: Waterproof (leak protection) system activated
causes: The leak protection system has been triggered. The programme stops and the drain pump runs.
steps: Close the stopcock.
Switch off the dishwasher and unplug it.
Wait for the drain pump to stop.
technician: Contact Miele service to find and fix the cause.

title: Circulation pump blocked
causes: The pump dried out and stuck after weeks or months without use, or on first use.
Less often, a technical fault.
steps: Remove the lower spray arm and filter combination.
Pour in 1 litre of warm water (max 75°C) with 3–5 drops of rinse aid and wait 5 minutes.
Refit the filters flat and the spray arm, then restart. Repeat 2–3 times if needed.
technician: If F78 persists, contact Miele service.
